pages: The derivative of f at x measures the instantaneous rate of change of f. It is defined as the limit of the difference quotient (f(x+h) − f(x)) / h as h approaches 0. To find where a function is largest or smallest, set the derivative equal to zero and check the critical points. This procedure is called optimization.
A Riemann sum approximates the area under a curve by adding the areas of thin rectangles. The definite integral is the limit of Riemann sums as the rectangles become infinitely thin.

The fundamental theorem of calculus states that the integral of f from a to b equals F(b) − F(a), where F is any antiderivative of f. It connects the derivative and the integral as inverse operations. Evaluating an integral this way requires knowing how to differentiate, since you must recognize F from its derivative.

pages: A partial derivative differentiates a function of several variables with respect to one variable while holding the others constant. Computing a partial derivative uses the same rules as the ordinary derivative.
The gradient of f is the vector of its partial derivatives. It points in the direction of steepest increase.

A double integral adds up a function over a region in the plane. It is evaluated as an iterated integral: integrate with respect to one variable, then the other. A triple integral extends the double integral to a solid region in space.

docs.name: Week 9 slides – Vector calculus.pdf
pages: A vector field assigns a vector to every point in the plane or in space. The divergence of a vector field F = (P, Q) is the sum of partial derivatives ∂P/∂x + ∂Q/∂y. It measures how much the field spreads out from a point.
A line integral adds up a vector field along a curve. It is computed by parametrizing the curve and evaluating an ordinary integral in the parameter t.

Green's theorem states that the line integral of F around a closed curve C equals the double integral of ∂Q/∂x − ∂P/∂y over the region D enclosed by C. Using Green's theorem, a difficult line integral can be traded for a double integral over the enclosed region.

packs.name: Office hours memo (transcript).txt
pages: So the divergence theorem is the three-dimensional version of what we did last week. It says the flux of F out through a closed surface equals the triple integral of the divergence of F over the solid inside. Flux is a surface integral: you add up how much of the field passes through each little patch of the surface, and each patch is set up as a double integral over the parameters. Remember that divergence measures how much the field spreads out from a point, so the theorem is just adding up all that spreading.
